relations.note: Sydyk fathers Eshmun, presented as the eighth son and brother of the Cabiri.
Eshmun is the younger or eighth brother of Sydyk's seven Cabiri.

relations.myth: Astronoë pursues the beautiful hunter Eshmun
relations.note: Astronoë desires Eshmun and sexually pursues him while he is hunting.

relations.myth: Astronoë restores Eshmun after his death
relations.note: After Eshmun's self-castration and death, Astronoë revives him through life-giving warmth.

relations.myth: Astronoë raises restored Eshmun to divinity
relations.note: Astronoë causes the restored mortal youth Eshmun to become divine.
Astarte and Eshmun share cultic space and joint dedications at Bostan esh-Sheikh.

relations.myth: Modern identification of Astronoë with Astarte
relations.note: Modern scholars often identify Eshmun's pursuer Astronoë with Astarte, though Damascius is not explicit.

relations.myth: Gods jointly guarantee the Arpad treaty
relations.note: Eshmun and Melqart appear together among the divine guarantors enforcing the royal oath.

relations.myth: Gods threaten deprivation under the treaty curse
relations.note: Eshmun and Melqart jointly threaten to remove food, clothing, oil, and other necessities.
Eshmun and Melqart receive associated but apparently distinct worship in Cypriot dedications.
Sidonian theology makes solar Apollo father of Eshmun-Asklepios, allegorized as health-bearing air.
Greek texts and a trilingual dedication explicitly identify Eshmun with Asklepios.
The Latin version of the Sardinian dedication identifies Eshmun with Roman Aesculapius.
Hygieia is paired with Asklepios in a later Kition cult possibly continuing Eshmun's sanctuary.
